architecture_mapping.f2_target: WP1202 deterministic target-shaped Ubuntu twin materialization
architecture_mapping.reason: The current WP1202 source describes what the twin must preserve but intentionally performs no materialization. mkosi can build distro/package-defined OS images without becoming F2 state authority.
nspawn boots systemd in a container and is efficient for userspace lifecycle checks, but shares the host kernel; its receipts must explicitly deny guest-kernel/firmware/device/physical credit.

vmspawn provides a full VM boundary plus controllable CPU/RAM, image format/disk type, KVM, VSOCK, TPM, EFI NVRAM and Secure Boot surfaces that directly exercise hidden host assumptions excluded by an nspawn-only twin.

architecture_mapping.f2_target: portable/mature VM backend fallback and comparator
architecture_mapping.reason: mkosi defaults its VM verb to qemu. Treating qemu as an explicit peer allows capability-dependent routing and later ablation instead of silently changing fidelity when vmspawn is unavailable.

Ephemeral snapshots improve reproducibility and cleanup, but cannot prove update/rollback/reboot persistence across independently recreated VM instances. Persistent-image-copy scenarios must remain separate.
Missing host capability is infrastructure/fidelity evidence, not a product logic failure and not permission to weaken host security configuration automatically.

critical_mismatches.finding: An nspawn PASS cannot validate the target kernel, firmware, GPU/USB4 stack, KVM behavior or physical peripherals.

A full VM boot still does not automatically reproduce the target GNOME/Wayland/X11 user session, PipeWire/WirePlumber graph, portals, browser package confinement or real capture/display devices required by WP1203/WP1204.
mkosi/systemd/vmspawn are actively evolving; unpinned distro-default versions make a passing twin non-reproducible and can change semantics such as image, manager, ephemeral or firmware handling.
Using ephemeral snapshots for all scenarios can hide persistence defects by recreating expected clean state; persistent-state tests need their own explicit lane.
Host prerequisites such as KVM/VSOCK/user-namespace access must not be satisfied by automatic broad permission changes; the twin harness should report BLOCKED/DEGRADED with exact capability evidence.
If nspawn, vmspawn and qemu results are collapsed into one generic T1 PASS, F2 loses the exact fidelity scope needed by target-relative completion epistemics.

proposed_f2_shape.name: FRANKENSTEIN2_TWIN_BACKEND_PROFILE/v0
proposed_f2_shape.result_law: Each execution receipt binds exact backend profile + target profile + release candidate; no result may be promoted beyond its declared fidelity. Backend substitution requires a new receipt, never silent equivalence.
recommended_matrix: T4_PHYSICAL: separate target acceptance only; never inferred from any twin lane

integration_boundary.wp1202: Extend planning/schema only after Trigger-4 accepts the candidate; do not replace current UNKNOWN/fail-closed planner.
integration_boundary.wp1203_wp1204: Remain responsible for desktop/multimedia/device/session fault fidelity layered above backend boot capability.
integration_boundary.wp1207: Consume exact TwinBackendProfile receipts for clean install/update/rollback/restart matrices.
integration_boundary.unifieddb: May store admitted receipts/references; backend tooling is not a second truth store.
integration_boundary.effect_authority: No external tool invocation or host mutation is authorized by this E2 mapping.

hypothesis.statement: A typed multi-backend twin profile with an nspawn-fast lane plus at least one full-VM lane will detect more host-integration defects per unit cost than either a container-only twin or a single opaque VM harness, while preserving exact fidelity scope.

counterhypothesis.statement: The additional backend matrix may create maintenance/version burden without finding defects beyond a single well-configured QEMU VM plus deterministic synthetic fault injection.
counterhypothesis.falsifier: Run identical target-profile/install/restart/update/fault fixtures across NSPAWN_FAST, VMSPAWN_VM and QEMU_VM; compare unique defect discovery, reproducibility, setup failures, wall time, CPU/RSS/disk I/O and configuration surface. Retire any lane whose unique information gain does not justify its cost.
